Subject: MSA/Order Form: SLA redlines and maintenance carveouts

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the draft. Our legal team reviewed the MSA and the Order Form and attached a marked-up PDF with a few asks specific to SLA and support commitments. High level:

- Lumina needs an uptime target at 99.95% for the hosted API (global), with a clearer measurement window and agreed clock for downtime calculation.
- We propose a tighter P1 response time (30 minutes) for production incidents and a P2 ladder that mirrors our internal SLAs.
- We need explicit language around scheduled maintenance windows (max 6 hours per month, with 72-hour notice) and a carveout for critical security patches (4-hour notice allowed).
- Service credit formula: Lumina is proposing a progressive credit ladder capped at 20% of monthly fees; our counsel also asked for a trial-period exception for the first 60 days.

Attached: Lumina_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf (annotated) and an edited OrderForm docx with line comments. Ellen from counsel is CC'd — she can walk through the legal redlines.

Can we set up a 30-minute sync next week to run through the redlines and align on which asks are feasible?

Thanks,
Raj
Procurement Lead, Lumina AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Ellen Brooks <ellen@counselco.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: SLA redlines and maintenance carveouts

Team — I reviewed Lumina's marked PDF and have annotated our position below (summary only; line-by-line comments are in the attached PDF from our side).

1) Uptime target (99.95%)
- Acceptable for hosted inference endpoints, but we need to limit to production-tracked endpoints configured in the Order Form. We will not apply to test/dev or beta feature flags. Suggest language: “99.95% uptime for Production API endpoints as defined in Appendix A (measurement and excluded events).”

2) Measurement window and clock
- We prefer monthly rolling window measured UTC. Redlining: add explicit calculation example (total minutes in month - downtime minutes) / total minutes. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (as defined), customer-caused outages, force majeure, and third-party infra outages when verified.

3) P1/P2 response times
- We can accept 30-minute on-call acknowledgement for P1. We cannot guarantee full resolution in 30 minutes; we'll commit to the acknowledgement and an initial triage/update within 30 minutes and then a target mitigation timeline (e.g., 4 hours for mitigation plan).

4) Scheduled maintenance windows
- We typically provide a monthly maintenance aggregate cap (we can accept up to 8 hours/month for major infra work, but can agree to 6 hours if Lumina requires). 72-hour notice is standard for routine windows; for critical security patches, we propose a 24-hour minimum notice with explanation and a shortened notice clause for CVE-level emergencies (4 hours) with customer opt-out rights.

5) Service credits
- We push back on a 20% cap for every month (commercially aggressive). We propose a ladder with monthly cap at 15% for runtime credit plus one-time remediation credit if root cause is Redwood engineering regression. Trial-period exception: instead of a hard carveout, propose a graduated credit multiplier for months 1–2 (50% of normal credit) and full credits thereafter.

Next steps: Connor will load a sample traffic profile and run the Lumina CSV to show expected monthly credit impact. Lauren will propose operational language for the maintenance carveouts. Marissa and Ellen to align on exact redline text.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_response_v1.pdf (redline), SLA_credits_table.csv (modelled examples)

-Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2028 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: SLA redlines and maintenance carveouts

Raj / Ellen — operational clarifications from infra team:

- If Lumina needs 72-hour notice for all scheduled maintenance, we can commit to that for standard rolling updates. For security-critical CVEs we can commit to 4-hour notice windows but will include a short post-facto report and allow Lumina to delay non-blocking changes. We want to avoid an absolute prohibition on emergency remediation windows.
- Maintenance cap: we can accept 6 hours/month if Lumina requires, provided that we include an exceptions bucket for planned major upgrades (treated separately and scheduled quarterly with >14 days’ notice).
- Response SLAs: acknowledgment vs. remediation must be distinguished in the Order Form. Suggested phrasing: “Acknowledgement = initial response and triage; Mitigation = timeline to reach customer-impacting reduction.”

Operational ask: please confirm which endpoints and regions Lumina considers Production vs. Evaluation (we need to map to infra metrics to calculate uptime). Also confirm whether they expect 99.95% per-region or global aggregate.

Happy to cover in the sync — propose Wed Oct 12 at 10:30 PT.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
